rows.name: 5-HTP
rows.evidenceFor: falling or staying asleep in adults

lines.ask: 5-HTP: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who suggested 5-HTP to you?
lines.letGo: 5-HTP came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $15 a month?
lines.why: There are no good trials of 5-HTP for adult sleep. Evidence for mood rests on a few small, weak trials. It can clash with antidepressants.
lines.question: Is it for sleep, or for mood?
lines.instead: A short worry list before bed keeps the wind-down, no capsule.

safety.note: With SSRIs, MAOIs, tricyclics or linezolid, 5-HTP can push serotonin too high. A prescriber is the right person to ask.
5-HTP acts on serotonin, and mania has been reported. With bipolar disorder or ongoing mood care, start with a clinician.

rows.name: Apigenin
rows.evidenceFor: falling or staying asleep in adults

lines.ask: Apigenin: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Did apigenin come from a podcast sleep stack, or somewhere else?
lines.letGo: Apigenin came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $20 a month?
lines.why: No human trial has tested apigenin alone for sleep. In mice it acts on calming brain receptors. Chamomile, its main food source, has small trials of its own.
lines.question: Did this come from a podcast sleep stack?
lines.instead: Chamomile tea is the everyday source of apigenin.

rows.name: Bone broth
rows.evidenceFor: skin, joint or gut health in healthy adults

lines.ask: Bone broth: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What got bone broth into your day?
lines.letGo: Bone broth came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $50 a month?
lines.why: No trials yet test bone broth for skin, joints or gut. Lab tests found fewer collagen building blocks than supplement doses in research. Independent collagen trials showed no skin benefit.
lines.question: Is it the warm mug you'd miss?
lines.instead: A mug of miso or homemade stock keeps the warmth.

rows.name: Chlorophyll water (liquid chlorophyll drops)
rows.evidenceFor: clearer skin, energy or less bloating in healthy adults

lines.ask: Chlorophyll water: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did chlorophyll water first show up for you?
lines.letGo: Chlorophyll water came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $15 a month?
lines.why: Skin evidence is two ten-person studies of gels, not drinks. No trials yet test chlorophyll water for energy or bloating. Most drops are chlorophyllin, a copper-based form.
lines.question: Is it the green morning glass you'd miss?
lines.instead: A glass of water with a handful of spinach in a smoothie.

safety.note: Chlorophyll supplements have not been tested in pregnancy.
Chlorophyll supplements have not been tested while breastfeeding.

rows.name: Colonic or colon cleanse
rows.evidenceFor: general health, energy or weight

lines.ask: Colon cleanse: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who first suggested a colon cleanse?
lines.letGo: Colon cleanse came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $100 a month?
lines.why: No well-run trials support colon cleansing for general health. Case reports describe harms, and early weight loss from cleanses tends to come back. Your liver and kidneys already clear waste.
lines.question: What feeling are you hoping for after?
lines.instead: A week of more fibre, water and walks.

safety.note: Colon cleansing is more likely to cause harm with kidney disease. Talk with your kidney doctor before any cleanse.
Colon cleansing is more likely to cause harm with heart disease, partly through shifts in fluid and salts. Ask your doctor first.
Fasting and juice cleanses can swing blood sugar. Check with your diabetes care team before starting one.
Colonics and laxative cleanses can cause dehydration and salt imbalance, and case reports describe bowel injury.

rows.name: Consumer DNA wellness test
rows.evidenceFor: better diet or weight loss from gene-based advice

lines.ask: DNA test: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What got you to order the DNA test?
lines.letGo: DNA test came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $5 a month?
lines.why: One large trial found gene-matched diet advice did no better than advice based on current eating. Another, in overweight adults, found gene type didn't predict weight loss.
lines.question: Did the report change a single meal?
lines.instead: Keep the ancestry part; skip the paid add-on reports.

rows.name: EMF blockers and anti-radiation phone stickers
rows.evidenceFor: lower exposure or better health

lines.ask: EMF stickers: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you hear about EMF stickers?
lines.letGo: EMF stickers came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $2 a month?
lines.why: No evidence these reduce exposure. The FTC charged sellers over false claims, and lab tests found no drop. The FDA links no health problem to phone signals.
lines.question: What made the phone start to feel worrying?
lines.instead: Phone across the room at night keeps the calm.

rows.name: Evening primrose oil
rows.evidenceFor: calmer eczema or easier PMS

lines.ask: Primrose oil: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who first suggested evening primrose oil?
lines.letGo: Primrose oil came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $12 a month?
lines.why: Careful reviews found evening primrose oil works no better than a placebo for eczema. For PMS, the few trials are small, and the best-run ones found no benefit.
lines.question: What did you start it for?

safety.note: Evening primrose oil may raise bleeding with warfarin. Check with a prescriber first.

rows.name: Eye cream (alongside a face moisturizer)
rows.evidenceFor: more benefit around the eyes than the face moisturizer already gives

lines.ask: Eye cream: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who recommended an eye cream on top of your moisturizer?
lines.letGo: Eye cream came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $45 a month?
lines.why: A 2024 review found few trials of eye creams themselves. Ingredients like retinoids and caffeine have small studies around the eyes, so the ingredient matters more than the jar.
lines.question: Does it hold anything your moisturizer lacks?
lines.instead: Your moisturizer, patted gently around the eyes with the ring finger.

rows.name: Facial plus at-home LED plus microcurrent (all three)
rows.evidenceFor: more visible change from all three than from one alone

lines.ask: Facial, LED, microcurrent: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did a facial, LED and microcurrent all end up in your routine?
lines.letGo: Facial, LED, microcurrent came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $140 a month?
lines.why: No study tests stacking all three. Home LED has small trials for fine lines, monthly facials are untested, and microcurrent devices have almost no independent research.
lines.question: Which of the three would you keep first?
lines.instead: The one you would keep, plus daily sunscreen.

rows.name: Glutamine (L-glutamine powder)
rows.evidenceFor: faster recovery, more muscle or fewer colds in healthy adults who train

lines.ask: Glutamine: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who put glutamine on your list?
lines.letGo: Glutamine came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $20 a month?
lines.why: In trials of healthy people who train, glutamine changed neither strength, muscle, body fat nor immune markers. Protein-rich food already supplies plenty of it.
lines.question: What made you start taking it?
lines.instead: A protein-rich meal after training already brings glutamine along.

rows.name: Glycine
rows.evidenceFor: falling asleep sooner and next-day alertness

lines.ask: Glycine: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did glycine at bedtime come from?
lines.letGo: Glycine came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $10 a month?
lines.why: Small Japanese trials found 3 g at bedtime helped people fall asleep sooner and feel less tired. Each involved researchers from a glycine maker; no independent trial yet.
lines.question: Do you fall asleep sooner on glycine nights?

rows.name: Greens powder (AG1 and similar)
rows.evidenceFor: general health, energy and digestion

lines.ask: Greens powder: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did greens powder find its way into your mornings?
lines.letGo: Greens powder came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $79 a month?
lines.why: No independent trials yet. Every study so far was run or paid for by a greens brand, showing small shifts in gut bacteria and blood nutrient levels. Products like AG1 hold a multivitamin-level mix plus plant extracts.
lines.question: Is the morning glass the part you would miss?
lines.instead: A smoothie with frozen spinach and berries keeps the morning glass.

safety.note: Greens powder makers advise a doctor check while breastfeeding.
Greens powder makers advise a doctor check when taking medication, given the herbal extracts.
Greens powder makers advise a doctor check in pregnancy, as many blends include herbal extracts.
The AG1 maker advises a doctor check for anyone under 18.

rows.name: Grounding or earthing (sheets, mats)
rows.evidenceFor: better sleep

lines.ask: Grounding mat: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you come across grounding?
lines.letGo: Grounding mat came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $4 a month?
lines.why: Most studies are tiny and run by people tied to grounding companies. One small independent trial, in older adults with Alzheimer's, found better sleep scores.
lines.question: Do you sleep differently with it or without?
lines.instead: Barefoot time on grass or sand keeps the outdoor part.

rows.name: Hair growth gummies (biotin blends, such as SugarBearHair)
rows.evidenceFor: fuller, faster-growing hair without a deficiency

lines.ask: Hair gummies: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you first see the hair gummies?
lines.letGo: Hair gummies came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $30 a month?
lines.why: No study we found tests these gummies. A review found biotin helped hair only when an underlying cause like deficiency was present, and deficiency is uncommon.
lines.question: Have you noticed any change in your hair?
lines.instead: A dermatologist visit, if hair shedding is the real worry.

safety.note: These gummies hold biotin, which can skew some blood tests, including a heart test. Mention them before any blood draw.
Sudden, patchy or heavy hair shedding is worth a dermatologist visit, since it often has a cause worth finding.

rows.name: Hyperbaric oxygen (wellness use)
rows.evidenceFor: recovery, focus or slower ageing in healthy adults

lines.ask: Hyperbaric oxygen: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did you first hear about hyperbaric sessions?
lines.letGo: Hyperbaric oxygen came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $300 a month?
lines.why: Hyperbaric oxygen is real medicine for diving injuries, carbon monoxide and some wounds. The wellness studies, in adults over 64, came from a clinic chain that sells it.
lines.question: Is it the hour of quiet you'd miss?

safety.note: Ear and sinus pressure are common, and pure oxygen is a fire risk. FDA advises an accredited facility for any session.

rows.name: IV vitamin drips
rows.evidenceFor: energy, immunity and recovery in people without a deficiency

lines.ask: IV drip: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did you first hear about IV drips?
lines.letGo: IV drip came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $215 a month?
lines.why: No good trials in healthy people. A small placebo-controlled trial in fibromyalgia found no difference from a plain fluid drip. IV vitamins are standard care for real deficiencies.
lines.question: Is it for hangovers, or a general lift?
lines.instead: Water, rest and a decent breakfast cover most of it.

safety.note: Infections, some serious, have followed drips mixed in unclean conditions. A licensed clinic with a clinician on site lowers the risk.
Extra fluid and minerals can strain the kidneys, so a clinician check comes first.
Fluid overload and shifts in magnesium or potassium can upset heart rhythm, so a clinician check comes first.
Drips can swing blood pressure, and fast infusions can cause fainting, so a clinician check comes first.
IV vitamin drips haven't been studied in pregnancy, so a clinician check comes first.
IV vitamin drips haven't been studied during breastfeeding, so a clinician check comes first.

rows.name: Jaw exerciser (jawline trainer)
rows.evidenceFor: a more defined jawline

lines.ask: Jaw exerciser: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you first see the jaw exerciser?
lines.letGo: Jaw exerciser came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $3 a month?
lines.why: No trials. In a 2024 two-person report, three months of use changed nothing visible. Chewing muscles don't shape the fat or skin under the chin.
lines.question: Has your jaw felt sore since starting?

safety.note: If your jaw clicks, locks or aches, a dentist is the one to ask before any jaw training.

rows.name: Lymphatic drainage massage
rows.evidenceFor: less puffiness or better wellbeing in healthy adults

lines.ask: Lymphatic massage: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did lymphatic drainage first come up for you?
lines.letGo: Lymphatic massage came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $120 a month?
lines.why: The medical version is for lymphedema, and even there it adds only a little to compression. There's no good evidence it de-puffs people without swelling.
lines.question: Is it the de-puffing or the quiet hour?
lines.instead: A monthly massage you love keeps the quiet hour.

rows.name: Magnesium L-threonate (Magtein)
rows.evidenceFor: better sleep from the threonate form specifically

lines.ask: Mag threonate: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What drew you to this form of magnesium?
lines.letGo: Mag threonate came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $40 a month?
lines.why: Two trials, both paid for by makers of the Magtein form, found modest gains in self-rated sleep. Ring-tracked sleep improved in one and not the other.
lines.question: Did you pick this form for sleep or memory?
lines.instead: If magnesium is the goal, plain glycinate at bedtime, though its sleep evidence is thin too.

safety.note: With reduced kidney function, magnesium can build up in the blood. A clinician can say what amount is safe.

rows.name: Magnesium spray or oil (on the skin)
rows.evidenceFor: raising magnesium or better sleep through the skin

lines.ask: Magnesium spray: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you pick up the magnesium spray?
lines.letGo: Magnesium spray came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $12 a month?
lines.why: No controlled study shows magnesium crosses skin in meaningful amounts, and none has tested sleep. A 2017 review found the claims unsupported.
lines.question: Is it the evening rub you'd miss?
lines.instead: A warm bath, or a magnesium glycinate capsule if the magnesium matters.

rows.name: Microcurrent device (NuFACE and similar)
rows.evidenceFor: a lifted, firmer-looking face

lines.ask: Microcurrent: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did the microcurrent device come into your routine?
lines.letGo: Microcurrent came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $20 a month?
lines.why: We found no independent trial of a NuFACE-style microcurrent device. A 2024 review called the research scarce, and the one trial it cited tested a different electrical device.
lines.question: Do you still use it most mornings?
lines.instead: A two-minute face massage with moisturizer keeps the hands-on ritual.

safety.note: The maker says not to use it with a pacemaker or other implanted device. A clinician can advise.
The maker advises against use in pregnancy, since electrical stimulation has not been shown safe then.
The maker says it is not for anyone under 18.
The maker says to avoid inflamed or broken-out skin. Acne or rosacea that will not settle is worth a dermatologist visit.

rows.name: Mouth tape
rows.evidenceFor: better sleep in people without sleep apnea

lines.ask: Mouth tape: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you first hear about mouth tape?
lines.letGo: Mouth tape came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $15 a month?
lines.why: A 2025 review found ten small, low-quality studies, mostly in people with sleep apnea or mouth breathing; a few saw less snoring. None tested people who sleep normally, and taping is risky with a blocked nose.
lines.question: Do you snore, or is it more about dry mouth?

safety.note: No studies include children, and taping carries breathing risks.

rows.name: Multiple hydrating serums (two hyaluronic acid products)
rows.evidenceFor: more hydration from a second hyaluronic acid serum

lines.ask: Two HA serums: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did a second hyaluronic serum end up on your shelf?
lines.letGo: Two HA serums came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $20 a month?
lines.why: In a small trial, one hyaluronic acid cream raised skin hydration more than a plain cream. No study we found tests a second hyaluronic serum on top, and the second bottle is the same ingredient again.
lines.question: Do the two serums feel different, or about the same?
lines.instead: One hydrating serum, or a moisturizer that already has hyaluronic acid or glycerin.

safety.note: Skin that stays dry, itchy or cracked despite moisturizer is worth a dermatologist visit, since conditions like eczema can look this way.

rows.name: Mushroom coffee (Ryze, Four Sigmatic and similar)
rows.evidenceFor: sharper focus or calmer energy from the mushrooms at the amounts in a cup

lines.ask: Mushroom coffee: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did mushroom coffee first catch your eye?
lines.letGo: Mushroom coffee came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $45 a month?
lines.why: One small trial found 1.8 g of lion's mane sped one attention task. A popular blend splits about 2 g across six mushrooms, with about half a coffee's caffeine.
lines.question: Is it the mushrooms, or the gentler cup?
lines.instead: Half-caf coffee keeps the gentler morning cup.

rows.name: Retinol or retinoid plus an exfoliating acid on the same nights
rows.evidenceFor: better results from using both on the same nights than on separate nights

lines.ask: Retinoid plus acid: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who suggested a retinoid and an acid on the same nights?
lines.letGo: Retinoid plus acid came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $15 a month?
lines.why: No trial we found shows that a retinoid plus an exfoliating acid on the same night beats spacing the two out. Each can dry and irritate skin, and dermatologists note exfoliating alongside a retinoid can worsen dryness.
lines.question: Does your skin sting or peel on nights you use both?
lines.instead: The retinoid and the acid on separate nights, or the retinoid alone.

safety.note: Retinoids are usually paused in pregnancy, and an obstetrician or dermatologist can say which acid, if any, fits.
With rosacea, the AAD advises skipping glycolic and lactic acids, so a dermatologist is the better guide for this pairing.

rows.name: Salt lamp
rows.evidenceFor: cleaner air, better mood or sleep

lines.ask: Salt lamp: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did the salt lamp end up in your room?
lines.letGo: Salt lamp came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $1 a month?
lines.why: No studies. Clinicians note the lamps give off too few ions to change the air, mood or sleep. The warm glow is the real part.
lines.question: Is it the warm glow you like?
lines.instead: Any warm, dim lamp gives the same evening glow.

rows.name: Screens / phone in bed
rows.evidenceFor: winding down and falling asleep

lines.ask: Phone in bed: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: How did the phone become part of bedtime?
lines.letGo: Phone in bed came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go?
lines.why: The research finds no sleep benefit from a phone in bed. In 42 studies of young adults, heavier phone use, especially at night, went with later, shorter, worse sleep. A small trial found a phone-free half hour sped up sleep.
lines.question: What do you usually do on the phone in bed?
lines.instead: Charging the phone outside the bedroom, with a book by the bed.

rows.name: Sea moss (gel or capsules)
rows.evidenceFor: general health, skin and mineral intake

lines.ask: Sea moss: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Who got you onto sea moss?
lines.letGo: Sea moss came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $30 a month?
lines.why: No human trials of sea moss itself. Seaweed products' iodine swings widely, and lab tests found arsenic, mercury and bacteria in some sea moss.
lines.question: Is it the minerals you want, or the morning routine?
lines.instead: Iodised salt and a varied diet cover iodine more steadily.

safety.note: Sea moss iodine varies widely and can upset thyroid levels. Check first if you take thyroid medicine.
Iodine matters in pregnancy, but sea moss amounts are unpredictable and can run far above the safe upper limit. Ask first.
Lab tests found arsenic, mercury and bacteria in some store-bought sea moss. Quality varies a lot between brands.

rows.name: Second meditation or sleep app
rows.evidenceFor: added benefit from a second app on top of the first

lines.ask: Second calm app: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What got you a second meditation or sleep app?
lines.letGo: Second calm app came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $13 a month?
lines.why: One mindfulness app gives small lifts in mood and calm in trials. No study has tested whether a second app adds anything.
lines.question: Which of the two do you actually open?
lines.instead: Keep the one you open most.

rows.name: Second wearable (Oura plus WHOOP)
rows.evidenceFor: learning more about sleep and recovery than one device shows

lines.ask: Second wearable: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What got you wearing a second tracker?
lines.letGo: Second wearable came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $20 a month?
lines.why: We found no study testing whether a second tracker adds insight. Worn together in a sleep lab, Oura, WHOOP and Apple Watch each tracked total sleep well and stages only roughly, so two mostly repeat each other.
lines.question: Which one do you actually like wearing?
lines.instead: One device, whichever is more comfortable to wear day and night.

safety.note: If a clinician asked for a device to watch heart rhythm, keep that one and check before changing anything.

rows.name: Shilajit (resin or capsules)
rows.evidenceFor: testosterone and energy in healthy men

lines.ask: Shilajit: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What first put shilajit on your radar?
lines.letGo: Shilajit came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $35 a month?
lines.why: Every human trial found was run or paid for by a shilajit brand. Lab tests have found thallium, a toxic metal, in raw resin and capsules.
lines.question: Has your jar been tested for heavy metals?

safety.note: Choose a product tested for heavy metals. Lab tests have found thallium in raw shilajit and in supplements.

rows.name: Silk pillowcase
rows.evidenceFor: smoother hair and fewer breakouts

lines.ask: Silk pillowcase: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: What first sold you on a silk pillowcase?
lines.letGo: Silk pillowcase came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $3 a month?
lines.why: No trials of real silk on hair or skin. One small trial of a silk-like pillowcase found no fewer breakouts than cotton. Less friction on hair is plausible but untested.
lines.question: Is it for your hair, your skin, or the feel?
lines.instead: A satin pillowcase gives the same smooth feel.

rows.name: Toner (hydrating or balancing)
rows.evidenceFor: more hydration when a moisturizer is already used

lines.ask: Toner: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did toner come into your routine from?
lines.letGo: Toner came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $25 a month?
lines.why: In a small study, toner then cream hydrated skin about as well as cream alone. The AAD advises skipping toners with rosacea.
lines.question: Does skin feel different on days you skip it?
lines.instead: Moisturizer straight after cleansing, while skin is still a little damp.

safety.note: With rosacea, the AAD advises skipping toners and astringents. A dermatologist can suggest a gentler routine.

rows.name: Two exfoliants (a scrub plus an acid, or two acids)
rows.evidenceFor: smoother skin from a second exfoliant on top of the first

lines.ask: Two exfoliants: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did the idea of two exfoliants come from?
lines.letGo: Two exfoliants came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $15 a month?
lines.why: One exfoliant can smooth rough skin, and no study we found shows a second adds more. Over-exfoliating can leave skin red and irritated, glycolic and lactic acids raise sun sensitivity, and strong exfoliation can darken spots on darker skin.
lines.question: Which one leaves your skin feeling best the next day?
lines.instead: One exfoliant that suits the skin, used less often the stronger it is.

safety.note: Salicylic acid is generally considered fine for a limited time in pregnancy, and the AAD suggests checking with an obstetrician or dermatologist first.
With rosacea, dermatologists advise stopping exfoliation altogether, and acne that keeps flaring is worth a dermatologist visit.

rows.name: Unlisted subscription you're still paying for
rows.evidenceFor: any wellness benefit while it sits unused

lines.ask: Forgotten subscription: no independent evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Do you remember how this subscription started?
lines.letGo: Forgotten subscription came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go?
lines.why: A subscription only helps when it gets used. A large gym study found members often paid for far more than got used.
lines.question: Do you remember signing up for this?

rows.name: ZMA (zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6)
rows.evidenceFor: higher testosterone, strength or better sleep in people already getting enough zinc and magnesium

lines.ask: ZMA: little real evidence. Worth a look?
lines.origin: Where did you first hear about ZMA?
lines.letGo: ZMA came from someone else's routine, and nothing you've told us ties it to your days. Want to let it go and keep the $18 a month?
lines.why: Trials in men eating enough zinc found no rise in testosterone or strength, and two nights of ZMA left sleep unchanged. The magnesium inside is the part with sleep research.
lines.question: Do you take it for sleep or training?
lines.instead: Plain magnesium at bedtime keeps the ritual with fewer ingredients.

safety.note: ZMA holds about 30 mg of zinc. Years of high zinc can lower copper, and a multivitamin adds more zinc on top.

rows.name: Alcohol in the evening
rows.evidenceFor: less REM sleep after evening drinks, already at two or fewer and growing with each one

lines.swap: Evening drinks doesn't sound like it's giving you much. Same plans, with the last drink a little earlier or the second one alcohol-free. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Across 27 studies, up to about two drinks already trimmed REM sleep, and more drinks trimmed more. Overnight heart rate also climbs with each drink. Falling asleep faster showed up only around five drinks.
lines.question: Mostly with friends, or more of a solo wind-down?
lines.instead: Same plans, with the last drink a little earlier or the second one alcohol-free.

safety.note: CDC calls not drinking the safest choice while breastfeeding, with at least two hours per drink before nursing.
With insulin or similar medicines, alcohol can bring on low blood sugar hours later, so glucose checks after drinking matter.
Heavy drinking strains the liver, so any liver condition makes alcohol a question for a clinician first.
Alcohol can deepen low mood, anxiety and sleep trouble, and interacts with some psychiatric medicines. If cutting back feels hard, that's a conversation for a clinician.
Alcohol interacts with many common medicines, from sleep aids to pain relievers, so a pharmacist check comes first.
US labels carry the Surgeon General's advice against alcohol in pregnancy because of the risk of birth defects.
Distill leaves alcohol out entirely below the legal drinking age, which is 21 in the US.

rows.name: Checking the sleep score every morning
rows.evidenceFor: how the morning number shapes mood, energy and sleep worry

lines.swap: Morning sleep check doesn't sound like it's giving you much. A weekly look at trends, with the daily score hidden. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Trackers mostly feel good to use. In small experiments, a fake low score left people with insomnia feeling less alert that day; in healthy sleepers, one low score didn't change sleep. Score worry tends to cluster with insomnia.
lines.question: Does the score change how the day feels?
lines.instead: A weekly look at trends, with the daily score hidden.

safety.note: With insomnia or anxiety, a daily score can add worry; hiding it for a while is worth raising with a clinician.

rows.name: Coffee after 2pm
rows.evidenceFor: shorter, lighter sleep when caffeine is taken within about nine hours of bed

lines.swap: Afternoon coffee doesn't sound like it's giving you much. A decaf, half-caf or black tea keeps the afternoon break with far less caffeine. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Across 24 studies, caffeine cost about 45 minutes of sleep and some deep sleep, more when taken later or in bigger doses. A regular cup's cut-off sits around nine hours before bed, and the loss is easy to miss.
lines.question: Is the afternoon cup about the caffeine or the break?
lines.instead: A decaf, half-caf or black tea keeps the afternoon break with far less caffeine.

safety.note: FDA suggests talking with a provider about caffeine limits while breastfeeding.
Some medicines, including certain antidepressants and birth control pills, slow caffeine clearance, so an afternoon cup can linger longer.
Pregnancy guidance keeps caffeine to about 200 mg a day in total, which one large coffee can reach.

rows.name: Dessert or sweets right before bed
rows.evidenceFor: lighter, more broken sleep when sweets come within an hour of bed

lines.swap: Late dessert doesn't sound like it's giving you much. Dessert right after dinner keeps the sweet, with more time before bed. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Eating within an hour of bed was linked to more night waking. A small study tied more daily sugar to more night arousals. Most of this is observed, not tested.
lines.question: Is the late dessert a want, or a habit?
lines.instead: Dessert right after dinner keeps the sweet, with more time before bed.

rows.name: Energy drinks (Red Bull, Monster, Celsius and similar)
rows.evidenceFor: shorter, lighter sleep from the caffeine, growing the later in the day a can is drunk

lines.swap: Energy drinks doesn't sound like it's giving you much. A smaller can before 2pm, or a cold sparkling water when it's mostly the fizz. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: The caffeine trims sleep just as coffee's does, and some cans hold three cups' worth. Students who drank energy drinks more often slept less and woke more. Blood pressure also rises for a few hours after a can.
lines.question: Roughly what time is the last can of the day?
lines.instead: A smaller can before 2pm, or a cold sparkling water when it's mostly the fizz.

safety.note: A single energy drink raised blood pressure by a few points for hours, so with high blood pressure a check comes first.
FDA suggests talking with a provider about caffeine limits while breastfeeding.
Large servings lengthened a heart rhythm measure (QTc) even in healthy young adults, so a heart condition means a clinician check first.
Some medicines make caffeine stronger or slower to clear, so a pharmacist can say whether a can fits.
Some cans hold over 300 mg of caffeine, past the 200 mg a day judged safe in pregnancy.
Pediatric guidance says stimulant energy drinks do not belong in children's or teens' diets.

rows.name: Late dinner (within 2 to 3 hours of bed)
rows.evidenceFor: more night waking when the main meal lands within about three hours of bed

lines.swap: Late dinner doesn't sound like it's giving you much. On late nights, a lighter dinner, with more of the day's food at lunch. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Findings are mixed. Surveys tie eating within three hours of bed to more night waking and reflux, yet a 10pm-dinner lab trial found unchanged sleep stages. One small trial saw lower nighttime heart rate with earlier meals.
lines.question: Late by choice, or is that when work ends?
lines.instead: On late nights, a lighter dinner, with more of the day's food at lunch.

safety.note: With set insulin doses, meal timing is part of the plan, so moving dinner is worth planning with the care team.

rows.name: Matcha or green tea in the afternoon
rows.evidenceFor: shorter sleep when afternoon caffeine lands within about nine hours of bed

lines.swap: Afternoon matcha doesn't sound like it's giving you much. Move it earlier, or pour a caffeine-free tea for the afternoon pause. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: A 2 g matcha serving holds roughly 60 to 80 mg of caffeine. Across 24 studies, caffeine shortened sleep; a 107 mg coffee needed about nine hours before bed.
lines.question: What time does the afternoon matcha usually happen?
lines.instead: Move it earlier, or pour a caffeine-free tea for the afternoon pause.

safety.note: In pregnancy or while breastfeeding, a caffeine limit is worth checking with your clinician.

rows.name: Nicotine pouches or vape
rows.evidenceFor: a faster heart rate after use, and lighter, more broken sleep when used near bedtime

lines.swap: Nicotine doesn't sound like it's giving you much. Daytime only, with the last one a few hours before bed. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Nicotine near bedtime makes sleep lighter and more broken, in overnight patch trials and in people tracked at home. Vapes and pouches nudge heart rate up.
lines.question: Did it replace cigarettes, or start on its own?
lines.instead: Daytime only, with the last one a few hours before bed.

safety.note: Nicotine nudges blood pressure up after each use; a clinician can help weigh what fits.
Nicotine passes into breast milk, so any plan for it is best made with a clinician.
Nicotine raises heart rate and blood pressure after each use, so changes are best planned with a clinician.
Nicotine reaches the baby during pregnancy, so any plan for it is best made with a clinician.
US law sets 21 as the minimum age for nicotine products, so Distill offers no timing or strength tips here.

rows.name: Second (or third) coffee
rows.evidenceFor: shorter, lighter sleep when the extra cup lands within about nine hours of bed

lines.swap: Extra coffee doesn't sound like it's giving you much. Half-caf or decaf for the later cup keeps the ritual. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Across 24 studies, caffeine cut about 45 minutes of sleep, and a 107 mg coffee needed about nine hours before bed. FDA calls up to 400 mg a day generally fine for healthy adults.
lines.question: When does the last cup usually happen?
lines.instead: Half-caf or decaf for the later cup keeps the ritual.

safety.note: In pregnancy or while breastfeeding, a caffeine limit is worth checking with your clinician.

rows.name: Weekend sleep-in (over 1 h)
rows.evidenceFor: making up for short sleep during the week

lines.swap: Weekend lie-in doesn't sound like it's giving you much. A lie-in kept under an hour, with an earlier night on Friday. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Studies disagree. In a Swedish cohort, short weekday sleepers who slept longer on weekends lived as long as steady sleepers, yet a larger device-based study found no benefit. A lab trial found catch-up shifted the body clock later.
lines.question: Is the lie-in for pleasure, or catching up on short nights?
lines.instead: A lie-in kept under an hour, with an earlier night on Friday.

rows.name: Work email after 9pm
rows.evidenceFor: what late work email does to switching off and sleep quality

lines.swap: Late work email doesn't sound like it's giving you much. One set check in the evening, then notifications off until morning. Want to try that swap?
lines.why: Studies following workers link more after-hours email with switching off less and lower measured sleep quality, not shorter sleep. These track patterns, not cause; in a small trial, a phone-free half hour before bed meant falling asleep sooner.
lines.question: Is it expected at work, or more of a habit?
lines.instead: One set check in the evening, then notifications off until morning.
